title: How do you expand a direct mail program into new audiences?
summary: New audiences are checking their mailboxes right now. Here’s how to grow your direct mail program into new segments and markets, one tested step at a time.
body_markdown:
Right now, people who would love what your brand offers are checking their mailboxes and have never heard of you. Direct mail can introduce you.


According to Lob’s[State of Direct Mail Consumer Insights 2026](https://www.lob.com/state-of-direct-mail/consumer-insights/2026-report) report, 48% of consumers say mail from a brand they’ve never purchased from increases the chances they’ll try it, and 45% say they’re more likely to trust direct mail from an unknown brand than a digital ad from one.


Here’s how to make mail work for your new audiences.


## Start with the segments you know


Look at which customer groups respond best today and describe what they have in common, such as purchase history or lifecycle stage. Use that profile to find similar prospects through list providers or lookalike audiences.


## Add addresses to your digital audiences


You may know many prospects only by email or phone. Appending physical addresses makes them reachable by mail.


SimpliSafe, a[2026 Lob Postmark Award winner](https://www.lob.com/postmark-awards-2026) , reaches a match rate as high as 90% by appending addresses to digital leads.


## Test small, then scale


Pick two or three promising segments or geographies and send smaller volumes to each. Give every group the same offer and format so you can compare results side by side. Grow the groups that perform and refine the rest.


## **‍** **Match the message to the audience**


New audiences bring new motivations. 58% of Millennials and 55% of Gen Z say mail from an unfamiliar brand increases the chances they’ll try it, compared to 31% of Boomers, so imagery and offers may need to shift by demographic.


Build flexible templates that let you swap products, offers, and images by segment. With[no-code design tools](https://www.lob.com/no-code-design-suite) , marketers can update those dynamic fields without waiting on a developer.


## Keep it repeatable


Standardize audience prep, templates, and approvals so each new segment builds on the last send.
